requirements.quote:
An authoritative name server is not required to verify that a zone is
   properly signed before sending or accepting a zone transfer.
requirements.condition: An authoritative name server sends a zone transfer.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is not required to verify that the zone is properly signed before sending the transfer.
requirements.why_checkable: The sending path can be checked for optional rather than mandatory prior signing verification.

requirements.quote:
An authoritative name server is not required to verify that a zone is
   properly signed before sending or accepting a zone transfer.
requirements.condition: An authoritative name server accepts a zone transfer.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is not required to verify that the zone is properly signed before accepting the transfer.
requirements.why_checkable: The accepting path can be checked for optional rather than mandatory prior signing verification.

requirements.quote:
However, an authoritative name server MAY choose to reject the entire
   zone transfer if the zone fails to meet any of the signing
   requirements described in Section 2.
requirements.condition: A zone fails to meet any signing requirement described in Section 2.
requirements.error_behavior: An authoritative name server MAY reject the entire zone transfer.
requirements.why_checkable: A signing-validation failure can be associated with an optional whole-transfer rejection policy.

requirements.quote:
An authoritative name server that



Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 15]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   chooses to perform its own zone validation MUST NOT selectively
   reject some RRs and accept others.
requirements.condition: An authoritative name server chooses to perform its own zone validation for a zone transfer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server MUST NOT selectively reject some RRs and accept others.
requirements.why_checkable: A transfer containing records with different validation outcomes can expose selective acceptance or rejection.

requirements.quote:
DS RRsets appear only on the parental side of a zone cut and are
   authoritative data in the parent zone.
requirements.condition: A DS RRset occurs at a zone cut.
requirements.required_behavior: The DS RRset appears only on the parental side of the zone cut.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Place the DS RRset on the child side of that zone cut.
requirements.why_checkable: The zone containing the DS RRset can be checked against the delegation boundary.

requirements.quote:
DS RRsets appear only on the parental side of a zone cut and are
   authoritative data in the parent zone.
requirements.condition: A DS RRset occurs at a zone cut.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the DS RRset as authoritative data in the parent zone.
requirements.why_checkable: Authority assigned to DS data can be checked against its parent-zone context.

requirements.quote:
DS RRsets appear only on the parental side of a zone cut and are
   authoritative data in the parent zone.  As with any other
   authoritative RRset, the DS RRset MUST be included in zone transfers
   of the zone in which the RRset is authoritative data.  In the case of
   the DS RRset, this is the parent zone.
requirements.condition: The parent zone containing an authoritative DS RRset is transferred.
requirements.required_behavior: The DS RRset MUST be included in the parent-zone transfer.
requirements.why_checkable: Transferred parent-zone records can be checked for the authoritative DS RRset.

requirements.quote:
NSEC RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative data in both the parent and child zones.
requirements.condition: A zone cut separates a parent zone and a child zone in the DNSSEC context described here.
requirements.required_behavior: An NSEC RR appears in the parent zone at the zone cut.
requirements.why_checkable: The parent-side zone data at the cut can be checked for its NSEC RR.

requirements.quote:
NSEC RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative data in both the parent and child zones.
requirements.condition: A zone cut separates a parent zone and a child zone in the DNSSEC context described here.
requirements.required_behavior: An NSEC RR appears in the child zone at the zone cut.
requirements.why_checkable: The child-side zone data at its apex can be checked for its NSEC RR.

requirements.quote:
NSEC RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative data in both the parent and child zones.
requirements.condition: An NSEC RR occurs on the parent side of a zone cut.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that NSEC RR as authoritative data in the parent zone.
requirements.why_checkable: Authority assigned to the parent-side NSEC RR can be checked against its zone.

requirements.quote:
NSEC RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative data in both the parent and child zones.
requirements.condition: An NSEC RR occurs on the child side of a zone cut.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat that NSEC RR as authoritative data in the child zone.
requirements.why_checkable: Authority assigned to the child-side NSEC RR can be checked against its zone.

requirements.quote:
The
   parental and child NSEC RRs at a zone cut are never identical to each
   other, as the NSEC RR in the child zone's apex will always indicate
   the presence of the child zone's SOA RR whereas the parental NSEC RR
   at the zone cut will never indicate the presence of an SOA RR.
requirements.condition: Compare the parental and child NSEC RRs at the same zone cut.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The parental and child NSEC RRs are never identical to each other.
requirements.why_checkable: The two NSEC records can be compared directly for equality.

requirements.quote:
the NSEC RR in the child zone's apex will always indicate
   the presence of the child zone's SOA RR whereas the parental NSEC RR
   at the zone cut will never indicate the presence of an SOA RR.
requirements.condition: An NSEC RR occurs at the child zone's apex.
requirements.required_behavior: The NSEC RR always indicates the presence of the child zone's SOA RR.
requirements.why_checkable: The child-apex NSEC record can be checked for an SOA type indication.

requirements.quote:
the NSEC RR in the child zone's apex will always indicate
   the presence of the child zone's SOA RR whereas the parental NSEC RR
   at the zone cut will never indicate the presence of an SOA RR.
requirements.condition: An NSEC RR occurs on the parental side of a zone cut.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The parental NSEC RR at the zone cut never indicates the presence of an SOA RR.
requirements.why_checkable: The parent-side NSEC record can be checked for the absence of an SOA type indication.

requirements.quote:
As
   with any other authoritative RRs, NSEC RRs MUST be included in zone
   transfers of the zone in which they are authoritative data.  The
   parental NSEC RR at a zone cut MUST be included in zone transfers of
   the parent zone, and the NSEC at the zone apex of the child zone MUST
   be included in zone transfers of the child zone.
requirements.condition: A zone containing authoritative NSEC RRs is transferred; this includes the parental NSEC RR in the parent zone and the child-apex NSEC RR in the child zone.
requirements.required_behavior: NSEC RRs MUST be included in transfers of the zone in which they are authoritative data.
requirements.why_checkable: The transferred records can be compared with all authoritative NSEC records of that zone, including its relevant side of a zone cut.

requirements.quote:
RRSIG RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative in whichever zone contains the authoritative RRset
   for which the RRSIG RR provides the signature.
requirements.condition: A zone cut separates a parent zone and a child zone in the DNSSEC context described here.
requirements.required_behavior: RRSIG RRs appear in the parent zone at the zone cut.
requirements.why_checkable: The parent-side zone data can be checked for RRSIG RRs.

requirements.quote:
RRSIG RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative in whichever zone contains the authoritative RRset
   for which the RRSIG RR provides the signature.
requirements.condition: A zone cut separates a parent zone and a child zone in the DNSSEC context described here.
requirements.required_behavior: RRSIG RRs appear in the child zone at the zone cut.
requirements.why_checkable: The child-side zone data can be checked for RRSIG RRs.

requirements.quote:
RRSIG RRs appear in both the parent and child zones at a zone cut and
   are authoritative in whichever zone contains the authoritative RRset
   for which the RRSIG RR provides the signature.  That is, the RRSIG RR
   for a DS RRset or a parental NSEC RR at a zone cut will be
   authoritative in the parent zone, and the RRSIG for any RRset in the
   child zone's apex will be authoritative in the child zone.
requirements.condition: An RRSIG RR signs an authoritative RRset.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the RRSIG RR as authoritative in whichever zone contains the authoritative RRset it signs.
requirements.why_checkable: The authority context of an RRSIG can be compared with that of its covered RRset, including parent DS/NSEC and child-apex RRsets.

requirements.quote:
Parental
   and child RRSIG RRs at a zone cut will never be identical to each
   other, as the Signer's Name field of an RRSIG RR in the child zone's
   apex will indicate a DNSKEY RR in the child zone's apex whereas the
   same field of a parental RRSIG RR at the zone cut will indicate a
   DNSKEY RR in the parent zone's apex.
requirements.condition: Compare parental and child RRSIG RRs at the same zone cut.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Parental and child RRSIG RRs at the zone cut are never identical to each other.
requirements.why_checkable: The parent and child RRSIG records can be compared directly, including their Signer's Name fields.

requirements.quote:
the Signer's Name field of an RRSIG RR in the child zone's
   apex will indicate a DNSKEY RR in the child zone's apex whereas the
   same field of a parental RRSIG RR at the zone cut will indicate a
   DNSKEY RR in the parent zone's apex.
requirements.condition: An RRSIG RR occurs in the child zone's apex.
requirements.required_behavior: Its Signer's Name field indicates a DNSKEY RR in the child zone's apex.
requirements.why_checkable: The Signer's Name field can be checked against the child apex and its DNSKEY record.

requirements.quote:
the Signer's Name field of an RRSIG RR in the child zone's
   apex will indicate a DNSKEY RR in the child zone's apex whereas the
   same field of a parental RRSIG RR at the zone cut will indicate a
   DNSKEY RR in the parent zone's apex.
requirements.condition: A parental RRSIG RR occurs at a zone cut.
requirements.required_behavior: Its Signer's Name field indicates a DNSKEY RR in the parent zone's apex.
requirements.why_checkable: The Signer's Name field can be checked against the parent apex and its DNSKEY record.

requirements.quote:
As with any other authoritative
   RRs, RRSIG RRs MUST be included in zone transfers of the zone in
   which they are authoritative data.
requirements.condition: A zone containing authoritative RRSIG RRs is transferred.
requirements.required_behavior: RRSIG RRs MUST be included in transfers of the zone in which they are authoritative data.
requirements.why_checkable: Transferred RRSIG records can be compared with the authoritative RRSIG data of the zone.
